title_en: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
title_zh: 俄罗斯报道乌克兰最大的无人机战争袭击，克里米亚地标桥遭到袭击
summary: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.
summary_zh: 俄罗斯表示，乌克兰一天之内发射了 2000 多架无人机，而基辅则收到创纪录的 17 次空袭警报。
body_en: Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit.

The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards the capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added.
Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people.
The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war.
The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions.

The structure - also known as Kerch Bridge - was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences.

Russian pro-war military commentators said on Telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate has responded to a BBC request for comment.

Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory, said on social media that authorities in Crimea were "bracing for further strikes" on the Kerch Bridge and that they felt Moscow did not appreciate the seriousness of the situation.

Ukrainian drones also hit several energy facilities, including an oil refinery in Ilsky, in the southern Krasnodar region, where falling drone debris sparked a fire and injured six people, including children.

Last week, President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of carrying out a concerted operation against Ukraine's bridges in order to "divide Ukraine... and make life as difficult as possible for people" on both sides of the Dnipro River which cuts across the country.
Despite the high-level diplomacy and visits by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to both Putin and Zelensky, peace remains a distant prospect.
Moscow is uncompromising on its demands for Ukraine to cede territory and give up efforts to become a Nato member.
The Kremlin has now also started to talk again about the need to rethink Europe's "security architecture", often intended by Moscow to mean a scaled-down Nato presence in countries close to Russia.

The apparent willingness of the US to engage in this conversation has set off alarm bells among Ukraine's European partners, which are concerned their continent's security could be redrawn by Washington and Moscow without their involvement.
A team of six - Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and a representative of the EU institutions - will represent Europe in future talks with Russia, Ukraine and the US.
But the Kremlin continues to be dismissive of European input.
"We have also said more than once we need to understand... how much their position will help the peace process," said spokesman Dmitri Peskov.

EU representatives kept pushing for "unconditional support" for Ukraine and "enhanced pressure" on Russia, Peskov said, adding that "this sort of wording rather suggests their reluctance to facilitate the peace process".
body_zh: 俄罗斯称，它记录了自战争开始以来最大规模的乌克兰无人机袭击事件，连接俄罗斯和被占领克里米亚的一座地标性桥梁受到轻微损坏，几家炼油厂遭到袭击。
官员称，俄罗斯军方在 24 小时内拦截并摧毁了 2049 架无人机和 4 枚火烈鸟远程导弹。莫斯科市长谢尔盖·索比亚宁补充说，仅飞往首都的航班就约有 600 架。
与此同时，基辅单日收到创纪录的 17 次空袭警报。俄罗斯的袭击造成至少 7 人死亡，对能源基础设施的袭击导致 5 万人停电。
几天前，美国、乌克兰和俄罗斯特使举行了旨在结束战争的会谈。
乌克兰战争始于2022年2月俄罗斯的全面入侵。
莫斯科任命的克里米亚领导人谢尔盖·阿克肖诺夫证实，无人机袭击了连接俄罗斯与附属半岛的克里米亚大桥，导致交通限制。
该建筑也被称为刻赤桥，是俄罗斯在 2014 年入侵并吞并半岛后建造的。俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京于 2018 年大张旗鼓地为它揭幕，并受到多层空中和海上防御的精心保护。
俄罗斯支持战争的军事评论员在 Telegram 上表示，这座桥不是受到直接攻击，而是受到了无人机弹头碎片的撞击。乌克兰国内安全部门及其主要军事情报局均未回应英国广播公司的置评请求。
在俄罗斯控制的领土内活动的乌克兰游击队 Atesh 在社交媒体上表示，克里米亚当局正在“准备对刻赤大桥进行进一步袭击”，他们认为莫斯科没有意识到局势的严重性。
乌克兰无人机还击中了多个能源设施，包括克拉斯诺达尔地区南部伊尔斯基的一家炼油厂，坠落的无人机碎片引发火灾，造成包括儿童在内的六人受伤。
上周，泽伦斯基总统指责俄罗斯对乌克兰桥梁采取协同行动，以“分裂乌克兰……并让横贯该国的第聂伯河两岸的人民生活尽可能困难”。
尽管美国特使贾里德·库什纳和史蒂夫·威特科夫对普京和泽伦斯基进行了高层外交和访问，但和平的前景仍然遥远。
莫斯科对乌克兰割让领土和放弃加入北约的要求毫不妥协。
克里姆林宫现在也开始再次谈论重新考虑欧洲“安全架构”的必要性，莫斯科通常的意图是缩小北约在俄罗斯附近国家的存在。
美国明显愿意参与这一对话，这给乌克兰的欧洲伙伴敲响了警钟，他们担心华盛顿和莫斯科可能会在没有他们参与的情况下重新规划其大陆的安全。
由英国、法国、德国、意大利、波兰和欧盟机构代表组成的六人小组将代表欧洲参加未来与俄罗斯、乌克兰和美国的会谈。
但克里姆林宫仍然对欧洲的意见不屑一顾。
发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫说：“我们也不止一次说过，我们需要了解……他们的立场将在多大程度上帮助和平进程。”
佩斯科夫表示，欧盟代表不断推动对乌克兰“无条件支持”，并对俄罗斯“加大压力”，并补充说，“这种措辞实际上表明他们不愿促进和平进程”。

title_en: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
title_zh: 五个欧盟国家宣布在卢旺达设立移民驱逐中心
summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
summary_zh: 德国、丹麦、奥地利、希腊和荷兰宣布为失败的寻求庇护者设立“返回中心”。
body_en: By Olivia Ireland and Bethany Bell , Reporting from Vienna
Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.
Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.

The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.
Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.

The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024 .
Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest".
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no "future or humanity", according to AFP news agency.
"I don't see any future or humanity in that. It's not the solution," Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported.
The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights.
The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.

In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.

In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda".
Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system.
Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants".
He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".

Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants.
The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".
With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration.
body_zh: 奥利维亚·爱尔兰和贝瑟尼·贝尔报道，维也纳报道
五个欧盟国家明年将在卢旺达开设一个移民驱逐中心，作为更广泛推动遣返行动的一部分。
荷兰和丹麦政府在声明中宣布，德国、丹麦、奥地利、希腊和荷兰预计将在 2027 年开设一个“返回中心”，准备接受转账。
各国表示，该计划将适用于在本国非法居留并可能被驱逐出境的移民，荷兰政府补充说，如果被驱逐者无法返回原籍国，该计划将提供替代方案。
各国表示，被驱逐者将能够融入卢旺达社会或返回祖国。
该计划将适用于那些已经用尽合法途径留在这五个国家的人，这与英国已取消的协议不同，该协议设想将人们送往卢旺达处理他们的申请。由于法律挑战，这项英国协议从未成功，并最终被 2024 年即将上任的工党政府否决。
唐宁街并未排除英国加入该计划的可能性，并表示他们将“饶有兴趣”地关注该计划。
据法新社报道，西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯表示，在卢旺达开设中心的计划没有“未来或人性”。
据法新社报道，桑切斯对西班牙广播公司 Telecinco 表示：“我看不到这有任何未来或人性。这不是解决方案。”
这五个国家表示，将移民送往国外的计划符合欧盟和国际法，但人权机构表示，这可能侵犯移民权利。
该协议是在欧盟最近进行改革之后达成的，该改革允许在欧盟之外建立枢纽。
周一在维也纳举行的联合新闻发布会上，奥地利总理克里斯蒂安·斯托克表示，这五个国家希望缓解欧洲庇护系统的压力，并阻止贩运者安排穿越地中海的致命旅行。
荷兰政府在一份书面声明中表示，作为协议第一阶段的一部分，这五个国家将“只返回单身男性”，并补充说，荷兰的重点“将是来自与卢旺达同一地区的原籍国的人”。
一旦到达卢旺达，人们将能够融入社会，这意味着他们将拥有居住权，以及获得教育、医疗保健、劳动力市场和法律体系的机会。
卢旺达内政部长文森特·比鲁塔表示，该国致力于与欧洲伙伴合作，为“移民提供安全、合法和有尊严的解决方案”。
他补充说，他们还将致力于“纠正全球经济机会的不平衡”，他称之为“非正常移民的关键驱动因素”。
在宣布这一消息之前，外交消息人士告诉法新社，该中心预计最初将作为试点运行，容纳约 100 人，五个国家可能分别派遣约 20 名移民。
联合国国际移民组织（IOM）可以发挥辅助作用。
国际移民组织发言人表示：“国际移民组织在向过境移民提供援助方面有着悠久的历史，包括在复杂的情况下。”他补充说，该机构正在与一些欧盟国家讨论“建立回返中心或类似机制的计划”。
随着几个欧盟国家选举的临近，各国政府一直面临着证明他们有能力控制移民的压力。

Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

In a statement released on Monday the five EU countries said “concrete negotiations with partner country Rwanda will begin for implementation”, saying the scheme would make “an important contribution to further curbing illegal migration, dismantling the business model of smugglers and relieving the burden on our population”.

Officials hope to send 100 people to Rwanda from early next year to test the model. The scheme will apply to adults whose claims to asylum have been rejected or others with no legal right to live in the EU.

In theory, according to diplomatic sources, migrants would stay in a reception centre in Rwanda for a couple of months, before choosing to integrate into life in the Great Lakes country or return to their home nation.
Unlike the failed scheme pursued by the British Conservative government in Rwanda, or Italy’s agreement with Albania , it will not apply to people pursuing asylum claims.

The reception centre, which would be an open facility, was not intended to house people long term but to accommodate regular flows of people, the countries said. Diplomatic sources said the EU countries were not using British-funded facilities built in Kigali.
The governments involved argue it will protect the European asylum system while removing the incentive for irregular migrants to come to Europe .
Denmark’s immigration minister, Morten Bødskov, whose government has pioneered a tough line on migration widely emulated across the EU, said it was “a huge breakthrough”.

The German interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, said: “Return hubs offer a positive approach for people without the right to stay and with no prospects in Europe, whose countries of origin do not cooperate in the repatriation process.”

Andy Burnham told reporters last week that the UK had not had direct discussions with European governments involved in return hubs but “we will watch that with interest, learning from what went on in the past. The public want us to do whatever we can to deal with illegal immigration.”

Critics have highlighted the ethical difficulties of striking an agreement with Rwanda’s repressive government , which was found in 2024 by the US state department to allow state security forces and civilian officials to commit human rights abuses with impunity, while also raising concerns about freedom of expression and forced labour.

The French Green MEP Mélissa Camara denounced the agreement between the five countries and Rwanda as “an agreement of shame” and “a grave moral failing”. She said: “Under this agreement, people will be deported thousands of kilometres away from the European Union , with no guarantees regarding the compliance with their rights.”

Alain Berset, the secretary general of the Council of Europe, the continent’s human rights body, said it was not possible “to be so precise a priori” about what any return hubs proposal meant. Speaking to the Guardian before the announcement, he said all members of the Council of Europe were committed to the European convention on human rights “and this must be the lighthouse” for all discussions on return hubs.
“On concrete cases, then we will have to see if this is compliant with the convention,” he said. He stressed that “all countries must be able to define their migration policy”.
Officials involved in setting up the migration centres expect legal challenges, but say the scheme is grounded in human rights law.

Rights organisations say the scheme is bound to fail. “Member states may call them ‘return hubs’ or even ‘welcome centres’, but no euphemism can hide the violence of uprooting people from the life they’ve been building in Europe, and sending them to a country they don’t even know, without family, networks or meaningful prospects,” said Chiara Catelli of Picum, a pan-European organisation that campaigns for the rights of undocumented migrants.

德国、奥地利、荷兰、丹麦和希腊可能面临被批评为“严重道德败坏”的政策挑战
五个欧盟成员国宣布计划在卢旺达为没有合法居留欧洲权利的人设立离岸中心，这是一项试点计划，预计将面临法律挑战，并被谴责为“严重的道德败坏”。
德国、奥地利、荷兰、丹麦和希腊这五个国家是第一个寻求使用欧盟新商定的遣返法的国家，该法允许那些已经用尽所有上诉途径反对被驱逐出欧洲的人被送往第三国。
欧盟五国在周一发布的一份声明中表示，“将开始与伙伴国卢旺达进行具体谈判以实施该计划”，并称该计划将“为进一步遏制非法移民、瓦解走私者的商业模式、减轻我国人民的负担做出重要贡献”。
官员们希望从明年初起派出 100 人前往卢旺达测试该模型。该计划将适用于庇护申请被拒绝的成年人或没有合法权利在欧盟居住的其他人。
据外交消息人士称，理论上，移民会在卢旺达的接待中心停留几个月，然后选择融入大湖国家的生活或返回祖国。
与英国保守党政府在卢旺达推行的失败计划或意大利与阿尔巴尼亚达成的协议不同，它不适用于寻求庇护申请的人。
各国表示，接待中心将是一个开放设施，并不是为了长期容纳人们，而是为了容纳正常的人员流动。外交消息人士称，欧盟国家没有使用英国资助的在基加利建造的设施。
相关政府辩称，这将保护欧洲庇护制度，同时消除非正常移民来到欧洲的动力。
丹麦移民部长莫滕·博德斯科夫(Morten Bødskov)表示，这是“一个巨大的突破”。他的政府率先在移民问题上采取了强硬路线，并在欧盟各地广泛效仿。
德国内政部长亚历山大·多布林特 (Alexander Dobrindt) 表示：“遣返中心为那些无权居留、在欧洲没有前途、原籍国在遣返过程中不予合作的人提供了积极的方法。”
安迪·伯纳姆上周告诉记者，英国尚未与参与回返中心的欧洲各国政府进行直接讨论，但“我们将饶有兴趣地关注此事，并从过去发生的事情中吸取教训。公众希望我们尽一切努力来应对非法移民问题。”
批评者强调了与卢旺达专制政府达成协议的道德难度。美国国务院于 2024 年发现卢旺达政府允许国家安全部队和文职官员侵犯人权而不受惩罚，同时也引发了对言论自由和强迫劳动的担忧。
法国绿党议员梅丽莎·卡马拉谴责这五个国家与卢旺达之间的协议是“耻辱的协议”和“严重的道德败坏”。她说：“根据这项协议，人们将被驱逐出距离欧盟数千公里的地方，而且他们的权利得不到遵守。”
欧洲大陆人权机构欧洲委员会秘书长阿兰·贝尔塞特表示，不可能“先验地如此精确”地解释任何返回中心提案的含义。在宣布这一消息之前，他在接受《卫报》采访时表示，欧洲委员会的所有成员都致力于遵守欧洲人权公约，“这必须成为所有有关返回中心讨论的灯塔”。
“在具体情况下，我们将不得不看看这是否符合公约，”他说。他强调“所有国家都必须能够制定自己的移民政策”。
参与设立移民中心的官员预计会面临法律挑战，但表示该计划是以人权法为基础的。
人权组织表示，该计划注定会失败。 “成员国可能称它们为‘回国中心’甚至‘欢迎中心’，但任何委婉的说法都无法掩盖将人们从他们在欧洲建立的生活中连根拔起，并将他们送往一个他们甚至不认识的国家，没有家庭、网络或有意义的前景的暴力行为，”Picum（一个为无证移民争取权利的泛欧洲组织）的基亚拉·卡泰利（Chiara Catelli）说。

title_en: ASEAN offers Myanmar's sidelined leaders a path back to summits, but says restrictions will stay until there is meaningful progress on its peace plan

summary: Southeast Asian leaders have agreed to engage Myanmar in stages after years of excluding its leaders from high-level meetings. The bloc says Myanmar could regain full representation if it makes progress on a peace plan.

body_en: ASEAN offers sidelined Myanmar leaders path back to talks
Southeast Asian leaders agreed on Sunday to engage Myanmar's government in stages, while making its return to high-level meetings conditional on progress on a regional peace plan.
Myanmar remains a member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) , but its political leaders have been barred from summits and foreign ministers' meetings since October 2021.
The military seized power that year, overthrowing the elected government led by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi and triggering a civil war that continues today.
In a joint statement, the leaders called for "a calibrated engagement with Myanmar through a phased and progress-based approach, taking into account developments on the ground.”

They said ASEAN could gradually restore Myanmar's full political representation if it makes "sustained and concrete progress” on the bloc's five-point peace plan. The plan has yielded little since it was agreed on in 2021, and fighting continues between the military and pro-democracy and ethnic armed groups.

"What more can we do for Myanmar?” Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. asked at the leaders' retreat in Manila. He urged the bloc to find practical ways to advance the peace plan and support an inclusive process led by Myanmar.

Leaders are also discussing trade, regional security and ways to share fuel supplies to cope with disruptions caused by the war in Iran. Australia and the Philippines signed a defense agreement on Sunday, while Canada and the Philippines announced on Saturday that they had concluded free trade negotiations.

A proposed code of conduct for the South China Sea remains unresolved. Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro said negotiations between ASEAN and China were 80% complete, but diplomats told AFP a deal was unlikely in Manila. Chinese Premier Li Qiang is representing Beijing at the summit.

US President Donald Trump is expected to arrive on Tuesday, toward the end of the summit, and meet the leaders of India, Japan and Australia, the other members of the Quad. The meeting is expected to precede talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday.
Activists plan to march against Trump's visit on Tuesday. Their protest is aimed in part at a US-backed industrial project north of Manila that they say could displace Indigenous families.

body_zh: 东盟为缺席的缅甸领导人提供重返谈判的途径
东南亚领导人周日同意分阶段与缅甸政府接触，但其重返高级别会议的条件是区域和平计划取得进展。
缅甸仍然是东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 成员，但自 2021 年 10 月以来，其政治领导人被禁止参加峰会和外交部长会议。
军方当年夺取政权，推翻了诺贝尔和平奖获得者昂山素季领导的民选政府，并引发了一场持续至今的内战。
在一份联合声明中，领导人呼吁“通过分阶段、基于进展的方法与缅甸进行有针对性的接触，同时考虑到当地的事态发展。”
他们表示，如果东盟在东盟五点和平计划上取得“持续和具体进展”，东盟就可以逐步恢复缅甸的全面政治代表性。该计划自 2021 年达成一致以来收效甚微，军方与民主派和少数民族武装团体之间的战斗仍在继续。
“我们还能为缅甸做些什么？”菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯在马尼拉领导人非正式会议上提出这一问题。他敦促该集团找到切实可行的方法来推进和平计划并支持缅甸领导的包容性进程。

活动人士计划周二举行游行反对特朗普的访问。他们的抗议部分针对的是美国支持的马尼拉北部工业项目，他们称该项目可能会导致原住民家庭流离失所。

title_en: Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests
title_zh: 将开普敦狒狒转移到保护区引发激烈抗议
summary: Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people oppose
summary_zh: 示威者试图阻止载有狒狒的车辆，当局称捕获狒狒是为了保护灵长类动物和人类。
body_en: Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests | South Africa
Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human

The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.
‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys

The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved.

The growth in both baboon and human populations in Cape Town in recent years has led to increased conflict and more baboons dying as a result. Meanwhile, a heated debate has raged between people who believe that baboons and humans can coexist and those who argue that baboons in urban areas are in danger and in some cases need to be relocated. Some animal rights activists have compared authorities’ baboon management to apartheid.
During Friday’s relocation, outraged protesters tried to stop vehicles taking the baboons away. One person sprayed a fire extinguisher, according to the Daily Maverick , a local news outlet.

After the confrontation, the local Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals branch urged those opposed to the baboons’ capture not to try to stop the vehicles. “Capture and transport are already stressful for the baboons,” it said in a statement . “Delaying their arrival prolongs their time in crates and risks adding to that stress – this is not fair on the baboons.”
It said it remained opposed to the baboon’s relocation, adding: “Our presence did not imply support … our inspectors are present because the animals need someone looking out for them.”

On Sunday, dozens of people sat outside the wildlife centre in a silent protest, some tying flowers to the fence. Baboons from a different troop also gathered at the boundary, calling to the newly captive animals, the Daily Maverick reported.

“We stand together for the Seaforth and Waterfall troops, for their freedom, their dignity and their right to live as wild animals,” Mandy Neal, the administrator of the Save Kogelfontein Baboons Facebook group, posted on Monday, calling for weekly Sunday silent protests. “ Our message is simple: CAPTIVITY IS NOT CONSERVATION.”

The City of Cape Town said in a statement on Sunday that the relocation had been successful, with the baboons being monitored 24/7 after being checked by vets and the females receiving contraceptive implants.

It said: “The Waterfall troop has been relocated due to the severity and persistence of human-baboon conflict in the Simon’s Town urban environment, the limited available natural low-lying habitat, the increasing risk to the baboons’ welfare, and public safety concerns … [and] as a very last resort after other interventions were evaluated and deemed ineffective, and as an alternative to culling.”

Prof Justin O’Riain, a behavioural ecologist at the University of Cape Town, said the baboon management plan had undergone two years of public consultations. “It has thus been disappointing watching members of the public and select NGOs, many which did not engage in the stakeholder process, now compromising the safety and welfare of the baboons and people through violent actions directed at staff and baboons in transit.”
body_zh: 开普敦狒狒迁往庇护所引发激烈抗议南非
示威者试图阻止载有狒狒的车辆，当局称捕获狒狒是为了保护灵长类动物和人类
将开普敦的一群狒狒转移到野生动物保护区引发了当地人反对捕获它们的强烈抗议，官员们认为这对于阻止该市人类与野生动物的冲突是必要的。
“满是狒狒粪便的房子很难卖掉”：开普敦对清除猴子的计划存在分歧
这支由 44 名成员组成的瀑布部队（以他们主要居住的地区命名）于周五和周六在南部海滨郊区西蒙镇被抓获。第二支规模较小的西福斯部队也将被转移。
近年来，开普敦狒狒和人类数量的增长导致冲突加剧，导致更多狒狒死亡。与此同时，相信狒狒和人类可以共存的人和认为城市地区的狒狒处于危险之中并且在某些情况下需要重新安置的人之间展开了激烈的争论。一些动物权利活动人士将当局对狒狒的管理与种族隔离进行了比较。
在周五的搬迁过程中，愤怒的抗议者试图阻止运走狒狒的车辆。据当地新闻媒体《Daily Maverick》报道，一名人员喷洒了灭火器。
冲突发生后，当地防止虐待动物协会分支机构敦促那些反对捕获狒狒的人不要试图阻止车辆。 “捕获和运输对狒狒来说已经是一个压力，”它在一份声明中说。 “推迟它们的到达会延长它们在板条箱中的时间，并有可能增加压力——这对狒狒来说不公平。”
它表示仍然反对狒狒搬迁，并补充道：“我们的存在并不意味着支持......我们的检查员在场是因为这些动物需要有人照顾它们。”
周日，数十人坐在野生动物中心外进行无声抗议，一些人将鲜花绑在栅栏上。据《每日特立独行》报道，来自不同种群的狒狒也聚集在边界处，向新捕获的动物发出呼唤。
拯救科格尔方丹狒狒 Facebook 群组管理员曼迪·尼尔 (Mandy Neal) 周一发帖称，“我们支持 Seaforth 和 Waterfall 部队，支持他们的自由、尊严和像野生动物一样生活的权利”，呼吁每周日举行无声抗议。 “我们的信息很简单：圈养不是保护。”
开普敦市周日在一份声明中表示，搬迁工作取得了成功，狒狒在经过兽医检查后受到全天候（24/7）监测，雌性狒狒接受了避孕植入物。
报告称：“由于西蒙镇城市环境中人与狒狒冲突的严重性和持续性、可用的自然低洼栖息地有限、狒狒福利风险日益增加以及公共安全问题……瀑布部队已被重新安置……[并且]作为其他干预措施经过评估并被认为无效后的最后手段，以及作为扑杀的替代方案。”
开普敦大学行为生态学家贾斯汀·奥里恩教授表示，狒狒管理计划已经经过了两年的公众咨询。 “因此，看到公众和特定的非政府组织（其中许多没有参与利益相关者进程）现在通过针对工作人员和过境狒狒的暴力行为，损害了狒狒和人们的安全和福利，这令人失望。”

title_en: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
title_zh: 由于特朗普支持恢复前首席执行官的努力，英伟达驳回了“让詹森回来”的活动
summary: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
summary_zh: 许多科技人士支持要求这家人工智能芯片巨头让黄仁勋恢复工作的努力。
body_en: Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, backed the effort.
Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, adding to a list of supporters who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign.
Fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return.

But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in bringing him back after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy.
Meanwhile on Monday, the Trump administration said it will further restrict China's ​access to AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. Since his departure, supporters have launched an online petition demanding his return.
Musk and Sweeny are among the more than 175,000 who have signed the open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.

The "Stand with Jensen" campaign claims to have been launched by a make up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, all demanding the return of the former chief executive.
They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".
President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.
"I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.
The Trump administration on Monday also issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models.
The move came ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jingping this week.

The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted to China.

Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.
The scandal-hit tech boss was discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times , external , though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him.
A representative for Huang declined to comment on the report.
The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.
President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal erupted, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".
Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.
body_zh: 英伟达驳回了一项要求黄仁勋交回职位的活动，因为包括美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在内的盟友支持这一努力。
特朗普周一表示，如果黄仁勋复职，他“当然不会介意”，这又增加了支持“让詹森回来”运动的支持者名单。
包括 SpaceX 的埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和《堡垒之夜》制造商 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 在内的其他科技巨头也支持黄仁勋的回归。
但英国广播公司获悉，这家人工智能芯片巨头的董事会无意让他回归，因为他上周辞职，因为他有两起婚外情，其中一桩涉及一名疑似中国间谍。
与此同时，特朗普政府周一表示，将进一步限制中国获取英伟达等公司的人工智能芯片。
所报道的事件给世界上最有价值的公司之一——一家人工智能领域的核心公司以及美国与中国争夺主导地位的斗争——造成了一场危机。自从他离开后，支持者发起了在线请愿活动，要求他返回。
马斯克和斯威尼是超过 175,000 人签署公开信的人之一，呼吁董事会在正在进行的内部调查期间恢复黄的职位。
“与詹森站在一起”活动声称是由英伟达现任和前任员工、合作伙伴、股东和支持者发起的，他们都要求这位前首席执行官回归。
他们对这位前英伟达老板“在没有经过有意义的正当程序的情况下被解雇”表示担忧。
特朗普总统周一对黄的未来发表了看法，称他“当然不介意”看到这位前老板重新获得职位。
“我想也许一个教训比另一个更重要，但我当然不介意看到这一点，”他在离开白宫时告诉记者。
特朗普政府周一还发布了对向海外数据中心出口芯片的新限制，允许中国公司获得先进的人工智能芯片来训练人工智能模型。
此举是在特朗普本周与中国国家主席习近平会晤之前做出的。
新规定将要求新加坡、泰国、马来西亚、印度尼西亚和巴西的公司申请美国最先进芯片的出口许可证，以减少这些芯片被非法转移到中国。
在涉嫌中国间谍的爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 事件曝光后，黄曾有望安然渡过难关。然而，在第二次婚外情出现后，他于上周四辞职，据称是与一位向他汇报的英伟达高管发生了婚外情。
据英国《金融时报》外部报道，这位饱受丑闻打击的科技巨头正在与心腹讨论重返英伟达的可能性，不过英伟达董事会并未考虑重新任命他。
黄的代表拒绝对该报道发表评论。
所谓的作战室也想获得白宫对黄的支持。
自丑闻爆发以来，特朗普总统一直热情地谈论黄，并且当英伟达前老板告诉他“不知道她是间谍”时，他也相信黄。
特朗普的观点与财政部长斯科特·贝森特不一致，后者呼吁英伟达从公司外部聘请下一任首席执行官。

title_en: Delaware hit by rare November tornado
title_zh: 特拉华州遭遇罕见的十一月龙卷风袭击
summary: Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado
summary_zh: 与此同时，严重的雷暴给阿根廷带来了棒球大小的冰雹。美国国家气象局证实，EF1 t
body_en: Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina

The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.

Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.
body_zh: 与此同时，严重的雷暴给阿根廷带来了棒球大小的冰雹

美国国家气象局证实，周四，一场 EF1 龙卷风袭击了特拉华州塞勒姆伍兹社区纽瓦克东南部。龙卷风宽达 160 米，路径长度为 4.4 英里（7.1 公里），估计峰值风速高达 100 英里/小时（161 公里/小时）。没有人员伤亡，但多处房屋的窗户和屋顶受损，一块大型酒店招牌掉落压在多辆汽车上，一辆半挂卡车在 I95 公路上翻倒。据美国国家海洋和大气管理局称，尽管特拉华州每年都会发生几次龙卷风，但这只是该州自 1950 年以来第二次在 11 月发生龙卷风活动。唯一一次有记录的 11 月龙卷风发生在 1989 年。
严重的风暴还导致阿根廷出现龙卷风和大冰雹。周五，一轮强雷暴席卷科尔多瓦省中部，冰雹大小达到棒球大小（直径约 7.5 厘米）。周六早些时候，该省部分地区在短短六个小时内就录得高达 73 毫米的降雨量。这种风暴在每年的这个时候很常见。来自亚马逊河与安第斯山脉交汇处的水蒸气迅速凝结，形成大量云层，通常伴随着倾盆大雨、闪电、龙卷风和大冰雹。

title_en: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
title_zh: 也门胡塞武装的推进可能进一步破坏全球经济的稳定
summary: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.
summary_zh: 英国广播公司的安全记者写道，伊朗支持的胡塞武装正在取得进展，他们的进展可能会产生危险的后果。
body_en: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels who seized much of Yemen in 2014 have now forced the army of the internationally recognised government to withdraw from the Red Sea coast in order to defend their interim capital, Aden.
Their advance bodes ill for Yemen's legitimate, internationally recognised government, its Saudi backers and, by extension, much of the rest of the world.
Yemen, a mountainous, heavily armed, intensely tribal and largely impoverished nation, sits at the far south-west corner of the Arabian Peninsula.

The country has two coasts: One faces the Indian Ocean on which sits the once-prosperous trading port of Aden, the other faces the Red Sea and, most importantly, the narrow chokepoint at the southern exit of that waterway - the so-called Bab al-Mandab Strait or, in English, The Gate of Tears.
Whoever controls that strait can threaten any or all maritime traffic passing through from both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.
In normal times, it accounts for around 12% of global trade, with anywhere between 70 to 150 ships a day making the transit.

But not any more. Although the Houthis say they are no threat to maritime traffic, they are currently at war with Saudi Arabia, making it extremely hazardous for the Saudis to send their oil tankers past the now rebel-controlled coast.

When the US and Israel started a war with Iran in February, Tehran responded by choking off much of the oil trade flowing out of the Gulf through another narrow chokepoint - the Strait of Hormuz. This sent oil prices soaring, boosted inflation and hurt economies everywhere.

The Saudis had a Plan B. Instead of exporting their oil past the dangerous coast of Iran, where their tankers risked being droned or mined by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, they started pumping it overland through their East-West Pipeline to an export terminal on the Red Sea at Yanbu. This worked for a while.
But then in July a cold truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis broke down, that pipeline got hit by drones and the rebels started firing missiles and drones at targets all over Saudi Arabia.

On land, the Houthis seized the initiative and made a lightning dash down the Red Sea coast, sending the Yemeni army into headlong retreat. A brief counter-offensive appears to have failed and the Houthis are now reported to be in full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the nearby offshore islands.

Nicholas Hopton, a former British Ambassador to both Yemen and Iran and now director-general of the UK-based Middle East Association, says: "The decision by the legitimate government of Yemen to prioritise the military defence of Aden at the expense of withdrawing from other areas suggests that the war is not going well for the Saudi-backed [Yemeni] government. And the rest of the world should be worried."

He warns that if the port of Aden – a city of roughly 1.25 million inhabitants – was to fall to the Houthis, it "would undoubtedly precipitate a further escalation in the regional crisis and further fragility in the global economy, catalysed by the US-Iran war".
But Mohammed al-Basha, the Yemeni founder of the US-based risk advisory firm Basha Report, believes the Houthis would struggle to capture the heavily fortified city of Aden.
"Any attempt to seize a densely populated city like Aden would come at a significant human cost," Basha said. "Advancing across the flat coastal plains would also expose Houthi forces to air power."
"For now, the Houthis appear to be seeking a negotiated surrender, hoping to exploit infighting and divisions among southern factions to achieve their objectives without a costly urban offensive."

It is conceivable that the Yemen war will settle into a less dramatic but deeply unsatisfactory stasis - a situation where casualty figures subside yet the country remains split between areas controlled by the Houthis - Iran's Shia allies - and the disparate and often poorly motivated forces of the Saudi-backed Yemeni army.

The former British defence attaché to Yemen, Col Iain Smailes, warned that the recent Houthi advance could trigger a spike in oil prices, as it did when they seized the Bab al-Mandab Strait in September.
He also warns this could have a knock-on effect to security well beyond Yemen's borders.

"By extending their control over the western coastline, the Houthis will increase their ability to smuggle weapons and ammunition from Iran, the Horn of Africa and elsewhere, posing additional threats to the region," Col Smailes said.
body_zh: 2014年，伊朗支持的胡塞叛军占领了也门大部分地区，现在迫使国际公认政府的军队从红海沿岸撤军，以保卫其临时首都亚丁。
他们的进展对也门合法的、国际公认的政府、其沙特支持者乃至世界其他许多国家来说都是一个坏兆头。
也门位于阿拉伯半岛的西南角，是一个多山、全副武装、部落人口密集且基本贫困的国家。
该国有两个海岸：一个面向印度洋，那里坐落着曾经繁荣的贸易港口亚丁；另一个面向红海，最重要的是，该国面临着该水道南出口的狭窄阻塞点——所谓的曼德海峡，或者英语中的“泪水之门”。
无论谁控制了该海峡，都可以威胁从地中海和红海到印度洋的任何或所有海上交通。
正常情况下，它约占全球贸易的 12%，每天有 70 至 150 艘船舶在此过境。
但不再是了。尽管胡塞武装声称他们对海上交通没有威胁，但他们目前正与沙特阿拉伯交战，这使得沙特将油轮驶过目前由叛军控制的海岸极为危险。
当美国和以色列二月份与伊朗开战时，德黑兰的回应是切断了通过另一个狭窄的咽喉要道——霍尔木兹海峡流出海湾的大部分石油贸易。这导致油价飙升，加剧通货膨胀，损害各地经济。
沙特有一个B计划。他们没有通过危险的伊朗海岸出口石油，因为他们的油轮在那里有被伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队无人机或布雷的风险，而是开始通过东西向管道将石油从陆上泵送到红海延布的一个出口码头。这工作了一段时间。
但随后在 7 月，沙特阿拉伯和胡塞武装之间的冷休战破裂，该管道遭到无人机袭击，叛军开始向沙特阿拉伯各地的目标发射导弹和无人机。
陆地上，胡塞武装抢占先机，闪电般冲过红海沿岸，将也门军队打得节节败退。短暂的反攻似乎已经失败，据报道胡塞武装现在完全控制了曼德海峡和附近的近海岛屿。
前英国驻也门和伊朗大使、现任英国中东协会总干事尼古拉斯·霍普顿表示：“也门合法政府决定优先考虑亚丁的军事防御，而不是从其他地区撤军，这表明沙特支持的（也门）政府的战争进展并不顺利。世界其他国家应该感到担忧。”
他警告说，如果亚丁港——一座拥有约125万居民的城市——落入胡塞武装之手，“无疑将导致地区危机进一步升级，并在美伊战争的推动下导致全球经济进一步脆弱”。
但总部位于美国的风险咨询公司巴沙报告的也门创始人穆罕默德·巴沙认为，胡塞武装将难以占领戒备森严的亚丁市。
巴沙说：“任何夺取亚丁这样人口稠密城市的企图都会付出巨大的人员代价。” “穿越平坦的沿海平原也会让胡塞武装暴露在空中力量之下。”
“目前，胡塞武装似乎正在寻求谈判投降，希望利用南部各派之间的内斗和分歧来实现其目标，而无需进行代价高昂的城市攻势。”
可以想象，也门战争将陷入一种不那么戏剧性但非常令人不满意的停滞状态——伤亡数字有所下降，但该国仍然分裂在胡塞武装（伊朗的什叶派盟友）控制的地区和沙特支持的也门军队的不同且往往缺乏动力的部队之间。
英国前驻也门国防武官伊恩·斯迈尔斯上校警告说，胡塞武装最近的进展可能会引发油价飙升，就像他们9月份占领曼德海峡时那样。
他还警告说，这可能会对也门境外的安全产生连锁反应。
斯迈尔斯上校说：“通过扩大对西海岸线的控制，胡塞武装将增强从伊朗、非洲之角和其他地方走私武器和弹药的能力，从而对该地区构成额外的威胁。”

title_en: Sudanese army air attack kills 13 in western Sudan: Rights group
title_zh: 苏丹军队空袭在苏丹西部造成13人死亡：人权组织
summary: 'Preliminary monitoring' shows women and children killed, homes destroyed in West Kordofan, says Emergency Lawyers.

body_en: Sudanese army air attack kills 13 in western Sudan: Rights group | Sudan war News | Al Jazeera
Share Sudanese army air attack kills 13 in western Sudan: Rights group on social media
An air strike launched by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) has killed at least 13 civilians in the Abu Qalb area of West Kordofan state, according to the Emergency Lawyers rights group.

Warplanes belonging to the military government carried out the attack on the Abu Zabad locality, with the victims including women and children, “according to preliminary monitoring” the legal collective said in a social media post on Monday. Al Jazeera was unable to immediately verify the report.

Several homes were also destroyed in the strike, which took place the previous day, Emergency Lawyers said. The group, which documents human rights violations and crimes in the war between the SAF and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), cited videos circulating of “horrific scenes” of destruction.

“The continued use of indiscriminate airstrikes on residential areas poses a direct threat to civilian lives and constitutes a grave violation of the rules of international humanitarian law,” it said in its statement.

Mohamed Didan, the official spokesperson for the Special Operations Forces that fight alongside the SAF, said on Facebook that his troops had moved through Abu Zabad and “eliminated” RSF positions in West Kordofan.
The war between the army and the RSF, which began in April 2023, has created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, according to several aid organisations.
Reports say the war has killed at least 59,000 people, displaced about 13 million and pushed parts of the country into famine.
Much of the fighting is concentrated in Darfur and Kordofan, although it recently shifted towards the Blue Nile province.
Drone warfare has also surged during the war, becoming the deadliest threat to civilians. Both sides are being supplied with drones by countries in the Middle East and beyond, experts have said.
The SAF has gained control over several strategically important villages and localities in West Kordofan recently in a push into the western reaches of the country .

title_en: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
title_zh: 法医专家表示，他对尸检照片的分析表明爱泼斯坦被杀
summary: Professor Michael Freeman tells BBC Newsnight that he believes the convicted sex offender's injuries are consistent with a homicide.
summary_zh: 迈克尔·弗里曼教授告诉英国广播公司新闻之夜，他认为被定罪的性犯罪者的伤势符合凶杀案。
body_en: This article contains distressing details and references to suicide
A forensic expert has said he believes that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's death in prison was the result of a homicide, not suicide.
Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Professor Michael Freeman said that after reviewing the New York City medical examiner's file he believes Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind.

The medical examiner who carried out the autopsy concluded in 2019 that Epstein's injuries were consistent with suicide and there was no evidence of the defensive wounds expected if his death had been a homicide.
Epstein was found dead in prison on 10 August 2019 in New York as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges.

Dr Barbara Sampson, chief medical examiner at the time of Epstein's autopsy, who ruled that Epstein's death was a suicide, has previously said: "I stand firmly behind our determination of the cause and manner of death for Mr. Epstein." The BBC has approached Sampson for further comment.
Freeman has served as a cause-of-death expert to attorneys-general in the US for death in police custody cases, including George Floyd in Minnesota.
He published his research and the New York City medical examiner's files after presenting his findings in London on Monday evening.

Freeman, who did not see the body, based his conclusions on the files and photographs from the examiner's report provided to him by Epstein's brother, Mark Epstein, who has always maintained that his brother was murdered.
Freeman said his analysis is independent and that he was not paid by Mark Epstein. His research has not been peer reviewed.

He told the BBC that he believed there are signs indicating an assault on Epstein, including a deep haemorrhage to his left shoulder and injuries that appear to be consistent to being struck in the face.
Freeman said he believed the evidence was most consistent with strangulation using a ligature and then that same ligature was probably used to suspend the body from the bunk bed.

He said there appeared to be fingernail marks above the ligature mark on Epstein's neck, which "would be consistent with strangulation, particularly from behind. And the attempt by the victim to try to remove the ligature from the neck".
He said "the injuries and the way the body was found don't match up. There's only one remaining explanation then, and that is that the death was as a result of a homicide."

The medical examiner who performed the autopsy at the time told the Department of Justice (DoJ) Office of the Inspector General , external that Epstein's injuries were more consistent with, and indicative of, a suicide by hanging rather than homicide by strangulation, adding there was no evidence of defensive wounds consistent with what is seen in victims of strangulation.
Freeman said he would have expected in an investigation of a death by hanging in custody for there to be a photograph before the body was taken down.

According to a DoJ investigation into Epstein's time in prison, the guard who found Epstein immediately called for a second colleague to help, lowered Epstein's body to the floor and began attempts to resuscitate him.
Epstein's death came a month after he was briefly placed on suicide watch, the DoJ report said.
When asked who might have killed Epstein if his interpretation of the evidence was correct, Freeman said he had "no idea".
"That is not something I have an opinion about. That isn't any part of any investigation that I've done," he said.
body_zh: 这篇文章包含令人痛苦的细节和自杀的参考
一名法医专家表示，他认为被定罪的性犯罪者杰弗里·爱泼斯坦在监狱中死亡是他杀而非自杀。
迈克尔·弗里曼教授在接受英国广播公司新闻之夜采访时表示，在审查了纽约市法医的档案后，他认为爱泼斯坦是被勒死的，很可能是从后面勒死的。
进行尸检的法医在 2019 年得出结论，爱泼斯坦的伤势符合自杀，并且没有证据表明他的死亡是他杀所预期的防御性伤口。
2019 年 8 月 10 日，爱泼斯坦在纽约监狱中被发现死亡，当时他正在等待性交易指控的审判。
爱泼斯坦尸检时的首席法医芭芭拉·桑普森博士裁定爱泼斯坦的死亡为自杀，她此前曾表示：“我坚决支持我们对爱泼斯坦先生死因和死亡方式的确定。” BBC 已联系桑普森寻求进一步评论。
弗里曼曾担任美国总检察长的死因专家，负责处理警察拘留案件中的死亡案件，其中包括明尼苏达州的乔治·弗洛伊德案件。
周一晚上，他在伦敦介绍了他的研究结果后，公布了他的研究结果和纽约市法医的档案。
弗里曼没有看到尸体，他的结论是根据爱泼斯坦的兄弟马克·爱泼斯坦向他提供的检查员报告中的文件和照片得出的，马克·爱泼斯坦一直坚称他的兄弟是被谋杀的。
弗里曼表示，他的分析是独立的，并且马克·爱泼斯坦没有向他支付报酬。他的研究尚未经过同行评审。
他告诉英国广播公司，他相信有迹象表明爱泼斯坦遭到袭击，包括他的左肩严重出血，面部受伤似乎与被击中一致。
弗里曼说，他认为证据与使用结扎线勒死最为一致，然后可能使用相同的结扎线将尸体悬挂在双层床上。
他说，爱泼斯坦脖子上的结扎痕迹上方似乎有指甲痕迹，这“与勒死相一致，特别是从后面勒死。以及受害者试图从脖子上取下结扎的行为”。
他说，“伤势和尸体被发现的方式不符。那么只剩下一个解释，那就是他杀所致。”
当时进行尸检的法医告诉司法部监察长办公室，外部称爱泼斯坦的伤势更符合并表明是上吊自杀，而不是勒死他杀，并补充说没有证据表明防御性伤口与勒死受害者所见的情况一致。
弗里曼说，他本来希望在对羁押中上吊死亡事件进行调查时，在尸体被取下之前会有一张照片。
根据司法部对爱泼斯坦入狱时间的调查，发现爱泼斯坦的警卫立即呼叫另一位同事帮忙，将爱泼斯坦的尸体放倒在地板上，并开始尝试对他进行复苏。
美国司法部的报告称，爱泼斯坦在被短暂置于自杀观察一个月后去世。
当被问及如果爱泼斯坦对证据的解释正确的话谁可能杀死了爱泼斯坦时，弗里曼说他“不知道”。
“我对此没有意见。这不是我所做的任何调查的一部分，”他说。

title_en: Nationwide ground stop could cost US airlines hundreds of millions
title_zh: 全国范围内的地面停留可能会让美国航空公司损失数亿美元
summary: Airline executives support modernising FAA systems as US Transportation Secretary Duffy seeks $50bn from Congress.
summary_zh: 随着美国交通部长达菲向国会寻求 500 亿美元资金，航空公司高管支持 FAA 系统现代化。
body_en: Share Nationwide ground stop could cost US airlines hundreds of millions on social media

Following the nationwide ground stop last week , United States airlines could face a financial hit of hundreds of millions of dollars even as airline executives press for increased investment in ageing air traffic control infrastructure .

The four largest US airlines – American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and Southwest Airlines – could face a combined hit of $345m to pretax earnings, according to brokerage firm Bernstein.
list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Trump denies responsibility for FAA nationwide ground stop
list 2 of 3 What forced the US to ground all planes? A router switch, we now know
list 3 of 3 After a nationwide ground stop, US faces aviation infrastructure questions

The effects of Friday’s ground stop continued to ripple through airline schedules on Monday, with more than 18,500 flights within, into or out of the US cancelled since the disruption began, according to FlightAware data.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told CNBC on Monday that the wider impact of the disruption could run into the “billions of dollars”. No official estimate of the total economic cost has been released yet.
Flights were grounded across the country for more than four hours on Friday, and the disruption continued to affect airline schedules over the weekend.

Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian also said the financial impact could run into the “billions”, telling Fortune on Monday that the disruption underscored the need for greater investment in the country’s air traffic control infrastructure.
Bastian pointed to the vast sums investors are putting into artificial intelligence and data centres, adding that the US should also be investing in its aviation system.
“We can’t even get $50bn to fix our skies,” he said.

United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby agreed that the disruption should be a “call to action”, saying the air traffic control system needed greater investment in modern technology to improve its reliability.

Transportation Secretary Duffy has asked US Congress for $50bn for air traffic control and airport infrastructure upgrades, an addition to the $12.5bn lawmakers approved for air traffic control modernisation last year.
The existing system relies on outdated equipment and needs a comprehensive overhaul, he said.
But Democrats have questioned the request, saying only about $1bn of the $12.5bn already approved has been spent so far.
On Sunday, US President Donald Trump called on Congress to approve the funding, arguing that the upgrades should be carried out all at once rather than in stages.
“We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs. Congress must approve,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
The funding debate is moving into a narrow window for congressional action. The House and Senate are scheduled to convene once more before the end of the year.

Speaker Mike Johnson has said lawmakers will take up the administration’s funding request during the current Congress’s lame-duck session, but Democrats have demanded more information on how the money will be spent.

继上周全国范围内的地面停飞之后，尽管航空公司高管敦促增加对老化的空中交通管制基础设施的投资，但美国航空公司仍可能面临数亿美元的财务打击。
据经纪公司 Bernstein 称，美国四大航空公司——美国航空、达美航空、联合航空和西南航空——税前盈利可能面临 3.45 亿美元的合计打击。

列表 3（共 3） 在全国范围内停飞后，美国面临航空基础设施问题
FlightAware 的数据显示，周五地面停飞的影响继续波及周一的航空公司时刻表，自停飞开始以来，已有超过 18,500 架境内、进出美国的航班被取消。
运输部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 周一对 CNBC 表示，此次交通中断的更广泛影响可能高达“数十亿美元”。目前尚未发布总经济成本的官方估计。
周五，全国各地的航班停飞了四个多小时，这种干扰继续影响着周末的航空公司时刻表。
达美航空首席执行官埃德·巴斯蒂安(Ed Bastian)还表示，财务影响可能达到“数十亿美元”，他周一向《财富》杂志表示，这次中断凸显了对该国空中交通管制基础设施加大投资的必要性。
巴斯蒂安指出投资者正在人工智能和数据中心投入大量资金，并补充说美国也应该投资其航空系统。
“我们甚至拿不到 500 亿美元来修复我们的天空，”他说。
联合航空首席执行官斯科特·柯比（Scott Kirby）同意这次中断应该是“行动呼吁”，他表示空中交通管制系统需要对现代技术进行更多投资，以提高其可靠性。
交通部长达菲已要求美国国会拨款 500 亿美元用于空中交通管制和机场基础设施升级，这是立法者去年批准用于空中交通管制现代化的 125 亿美元的补充。
他说，现有系统依赖陈旧的设备，需要进行全面检修。
但民主党人对这一请求提出质疑，称已批准的 125 亿美元中迄今为止仅支出了约 10 亿美元。
周日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普呼吁国会批准这笔资金，认为升级应一次性全部进行，而不是分阶段进行。
“我们已经开始了这项工作，但应该一次性完成，而不是一点一滴地完成。国会必须批准，”特朗普在《Truth Social》上写道。
资金辩论正进入国会采取行动的狭窄窗口。众议院和参议院定于今年年底前再次召开会议。
众议院议长迈克·约翰逊表示，议员们将在本届国会的跛脚鸭会议期间讨论政府的资金请求，但民主党人要求提供更多关于如何使用这笔钱的信息。

title_en: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children
title_zh: 林赛·克兰西因三个孩子的死亡将于明年面临重审
summary: The 36-year-old's first trial this year fell apart when a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict.
summary_zh: 这位 36 岁的男子今年的第一次审判因 12 人陪审团未能达成裁决而失败。
body_en: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial for deaths of her three children in March 2027 - BBC News
Warning: This story contains details some readers may find distressing.
Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her three children, will face a retrial next year, a judge has said, after a jury deadlocked last time in a case that gripped the nation.
The judge set a trial date for 29 March 2027, though the district attorney did not explicitly say what charges Clancy would face.
Prosecutors said they wanted a jury trial, and the defence said they took that to mean Clancy, 36, would again face first-degree murder charges.
Five-year-old Cora, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan were strangled at the family home on 24 January 2023. The defence argues she had severe postpartum psychosis.

"I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it's an indirect comment from the DA [district attorney] that they intend to proceed on first-degree murder indictments, so we will pick a trial date," defence lawyer Kevin Reddington said at Monday's hearing.
Prosecutors wanted a May trial date, but Judge William Sullivan decided on March instead. The judge is due to retire in June.
Clancy was charged in the first trial with three counts of first-degree-murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.
The district attorney has not yet officially said he will proceed with first-degree-murder charges. The BBC has contacted the district attorney's office for comment.

The prosecution could choose to bring lesser charges against Clancy, such as second-degree-murder, which applies to unlawful killings committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without planning.
A week ago, Judge Sullivan rejected a defence attempt to throw out the case on the grounds of double jeopardy.
Double jeopardy is a legal principle that protects someone from being prosecuted more than once for the same crime after an acquittal or conviction.
The judge's decision cleared the way for a second trial. It was Judge Sullivan who declared the mistrial on 4 September because of the hung jury.
Afterwards, some of the 12 jurors said in media interviews that they had been ready to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, but that one juror had held out.
It was not disputed at Clancy's first trial that she strangled the children with exercise bands in the basement of the family home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury.
She had asked her now-ex husband, Patrick Clancy, to leave the house to pick up takeout food and children's medicine shortly before the children were attacked.
The defence team wanted her found not guilty by reason of insanity, known in Massachusetts as lack of criminal responsibility.
The case sparked a debate over how postpartum mental illness is treated in the US.
Clancy is currently in a state-run psychiatric hospital and medical facility in Massachusetts.
body_zh: 林赛·克兰西 (Lindsay Clancy) 因 2027 年 3 月导致三个孩子死亡而面临重审 - BBC 新闻
警告：这个故事包含一些读者可能会感到痛苦的细节。
法官表示，被控谋杀三个孩子的马萨诸塞州妇女林赛·克兰西将于明年面临重审，此前陪审团在上次震惊全国的案件中陷入僵局。
法官将审判日期定为 2027 年 3 月 29 日，但地方检察官没有明确说明克兰西将面临哪些指控。
检察官表示，他们希望进行陪审团审判，辩方表示，他们认为这意味着 36 岁的克兰西将再次面临一级谋杀指控。
2023 年 1 月 24 日，五岁的科拉、道森、三岁的卡兰和八个月大的卡兰在家中被勒死。辩方称她患有严重的产后精神病。
辩护律师凯文·雷丁顿在周一的听证会上表示：“我想你可以从字里行间看出，当他们说此案需要陪审团时，这是地方检察官的间接评论，他们打算继续进行一级谋杀起诉，所以我们将选择审判日期。”
检察官希望审判日期为 5 月，但法官威廉·沙利文 (William Sullivan) 决定在 3 月进行审判。该法官将于六月退休。
克兰西在第一次审判中被指控犯有三项一级谋杀罪，即故意和有预谋地杀害他人。
地方检察官尚未正式表示他将提起一级谋杀指控。 BBC 已联系地区检察官办公室征求意见。
检方可以选择对克兰西提出较轻的指控，例如二级谋杀，该罪名适用于恶意或极端鲁莽但未经计划的非法杀戮。
一周前，沙利文法官拒绝了辩方以双重危险为由驳回此案的企图。
双重危险是一项法律原则，可保护某人在无罪释放或定罪后不会因同一罪行而被多次起诉。
法官的决定为二审扫清了道路。由于陪审团悬而未决，沙利文法官于 9 月 4 日宣布审判无效。
随后，12名陪审员中的一些人在接受媒体采访时表示，他们已经准备好以精​​神错乱为由判定克兰西无罪，但一名陪审员坚持不这样做。
在克兰西的第一次审判中，毫无争议的是，她在波士顿郊区达克斯伯里家的地下室里用健身带勒死了孩子们。
在孩子们遭到袭击前不久，她要求她的前夫帕特里克·克兰西离开家去取外卖食品和儿童药品。
辩护团队希望她因精神错乱而被判无罪，在马萨诸塞州被称为缺乏刑事责任。
该案件引发了关于美国如何治疗产后精神疾病的争论。
克兰西目前在马萨诸塞州一家公立精神病医院和医疗机构接受治疗。

title_en: Iran's growing exodus of young talent
title_zh: 伊朗年轻人才不断外流
summary: Conflict and uncertainty are driving more and more educated young Iranians to consider leaving the country.
summary_zh: 冲突和不确定性正在促使越来越多受过教育的伊朗年轻人考虑离开这个国家。
body_en: "I had actually decided to leave Iran back in 2023," a physician in her mid-30s, who wished to remain anonymous, told DW.

Her decision followed the 2022 death in police custody of 22-year-old Iranian-Kurdish woman Jina Mahsa Amini , who had been arrested by Iran's so-called morality police for allegedly violating the country's strict dress code .
Amini's death sparked widespread protests and inspired the " Woman, Life, Freedom " movement, which challenged authorities' enforcement of Iran's hijab mandate .

The physician said that the US-Israel war with Iran ultimately accelerated her plans to leave her homeland. She has been living with her family in a rented apartment in Turkey since early summer. From there, they hope to continue on to Germany .
"It took two years for my professional qualifications to be recognized in Germany. After that, I applied for an appointment at the German Embassy in Tehran," the physician said.
"Then the 12-day war broke out in the summer of 2025. The embassy closed and suddenly we were all left in limbo, not knowing what would happen next."

She became concerned after the US and Israel launched fresh airstrikes on Iran on February 28, 2026 — not just about the escalating conflict , but also about the prospect of internal unrest and political instability.

"Like many others we encountered during the emigration process, we decided to first move to a neighboring country," she said. "The plan was to stay in a third country for six months and then apply for a visa through the German embassy there. That's why my family and I came to Turkey."
Turkey is one of the few countries that allows Iranian citizens to enter without a visa for up to 90 days.
Since the latest conflict began , thousands of Iranians have crossed the border into Turkey. Many are trying to secure their stay through residence permits rather than seeking asylum.

According to official Turkish statistics, nearly 100,000 Iranian citizens were residing there in 2025. Among them are many academics and skilled professionals hoping to settle permanently in Europe or North America, seeing little future for themselves in Iran's war-hit economy.

A US naval blockade of Iranian ports ⁠in ⁠the Gulf over the past few months has disrupted oil exports, trade and government revenues. The turmoil has compounded the impact of decades of sanctions and economic mismanagement.
The situation has put most businesses under pressure by restricting access to foreign currency and raw materials, among other problems, threatening revenues and jobs.
The worsening conditions have left many people struggling to afford food, housing, health care and education.

The physician said the situation at the German embassy in Tehran, however, has improved in recent months. Some of her unmarried friends, who also initially moved to Turkey and spent substantial sums maintaining their stay there, have already returned to Iran to submit new visa applications from home.
She and her husband, however, have decided to stick to their original plan and wait out the six-month residency period in Turkey despite the difficulties.

"I can't and don't want to go to Germany without my family. I don't know how long it would take for them to receive family reunification visas," she explained. "And I don't know what might happen in the meantime. A new war could break out at any moment."

The departure of highly qualified professionals and students has become one of the most pressing challenges facing Iranian society. Today, there are few families in which someone has not already emigrated or is not at least considering doing so.
body_zh: “我实际上已经决定在 2023 年离开伊朗，”一位不愿透露姓名的 30 多岁医生告诉德国之声。
她做出这一决定之前，22 岁的伊朗库尔德妇女吉娜·马赫萨·阿米尼 (Jina Mahsa Amini) 于 2022 年在警方拘留期间死亡，她因涉嫌违反该国严格的着装规范而被伊朗所谓的道德警察逮捕。
阿米尼之死引发了广泛的抗议活动，并激发了“妇女、生命、自由”运动，该运动对当局执行伊朗头巾规定提出了挑战。
这位医生说，美以与伊朗的战争最终加速了她离开祖国的计划。从初夏开始，她就和家人一起住在土耳其的一套租来的公寓里。他们希望从那里继续前往德国。
“我的专业资格花了两年时间才在德国得到认可。之后，我向德国驻德黑兰大使馆申请了预约，”这位医生说。
“然后，持续 12 天的战争在 2025 年夏天爆发。大使馆关闭，突然我们都陷入了困境，不知道接下来会发生什么。”

2026 年 2 月 28 日，美国和以色列对伊朗发动新一轮空袭后，她开始感到担忧——不仅担心冲突不断升级，还担心国内动荡和政治不稳定的前景。
“就像我们在移民过程中遇到的许多其他人一样，我们决定首先搬到邻国，”她说。 “计划是在第三国停留六个月，然后通过那里的德国大使馆申请签证。这就是我和我的家人来到土耳其的原因。”
土耳其是少数几个允许伊朗公民免签证入境最长 90 天的国家之一。
自最近的冲突开始以来，数千名伊朗人越过边境进入土耳其。许多人试图通过居留许可来获得居留权，而不是寻求庇护。
据土耳其官方统计，到2025年，将有近10万伊朗公民居住在那里。其中有许多学者和技术熟练的专业人士希望在欧洲或北美永久定居，他们在伊朗饱受战争打击的经济中看不到自己的未来。
过去几个月，美国海军封锁了海湾地区的伊朗港口，扰乱了石油出口、贸易和政府收入。这场动荡加剧了数十年制裁和经济管理不善的影响。
这种情况使大多数企业面临压力，限制获得外汇和原材料等问题，威胁到收入和就业。
日益恶化的情况使许多人难以负担食物、住房、医疗保健和教育费用。
这位医生表示，不过近几个月来，德国驻德黑兰大使馆的情况有所改善。她的一些未婚朋友最初也搬到了土耳其，并花费了大量资金维持在那里的逗留，现在已经返回伊朗，从国内提交新的签证申请。
然而，尽管困难重重，她和丈夫还是决定坚持原计划，等待土耳其六个月的居留期结束。
“如果没有我的家人，我不能也不想去德国。我不知道他们需要多长时间才能获得家庭团聚签证，”她解释道。 “我不知道在此期间会发生什么。一场新的战争随时可能爆发。”
高素质专业人士和学生的离开已成为伊朗社会面临的最紧迫挑战之一。如今，很少有家庭中有人还没有移民，或者至少没有考虑这样做。

title_en: Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations
title_zh: 雷伊 (Raye)、罗莎莉亚 (Rosalía) 和多莉·帕顿 (Dolly Parton) 获得格莱美提名
summary: British singer Raye lands 11 nominations while Dolly Parton is recognised two months after her death.
summary_zh: 英国歌手 Raye 获得 11 项提名，而 Dolly Parton 在她去世两个月后也获得认可。
body_en: Grammys 2027: Raye leads with 11 nominations as Dolly Parton receives posthumous nods - BBC News
British singer Raye leads the charge at the forthcoming Grammy Awards with 11 nominations, while Dolly Parton has been recognised with three posthumous nods.
Raye is nominated for her latest Mercury-winning record This Album May Contain Hope and its lead single Where Is My Husband!, which is up for both song and record of the year.
Other nominees include Rosalía, Ella Langley, Olivia Dean, Ariana Grande, Bruno Mars, Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo, Miranda Lambert and Phoebe Bridgers.
Parton's two nominations, both in the best country duo/group performance category, come three months after the country music star died aged 80.
Parton is recognised for Butterfly, her collaboration with the Zac Brown Band, and Light of a Clear Blue Morning, alongside an all-star line-up including her goddaughter Miley Cyrus.
The late country star also received a nomination for best audio book, for her narration of Star of the Show: My Life on Stage.
The Grammy Awards 2027 will take place on Sunday 7 February in Los Angeles.
See the full nominations list on the official Grammys website , external
Madonna's album Confessions II, a sequel to 2005's Confessions on a Dancefloor, was absent from the "big four" categories - including album, record and song of the year.
That will be seen by many as the Grammys continuing their tradition of snubbing the US singer, but the album did make it into the best dance category.
Rosalía's nine nominations for her widely acclaimed album Lux come after her huge success at last week's Latin Grammy Awards.
Langley's seven nominations include song of the year for her breakthrough hit Choosin' Texas, which this year became the longest-running number one single in the history of Billboard's Hot 100.
There are five new categories being introduced, including best Latin song and best Asian pop music performance.
They have been added as part of the Academy's attempts to make the event "more inclusive" and represent a wider range of music genres.

However, critics fear that the new specialist categories will result in genres such as K-pop being under-represented in the major categories, and acts including BTS and Stray Kids have said they will boycott next year's ceremony.
Four of Korea’s five biggest entertainment companies withheld their music from consideration. Starship Entertainment, which bucked the trend, scored nominations for its girl bands IVE and KiiiKiii.
The other nominees were Babymetal, Japanese singer Lisa (not to be confused with the Blackpink star of the same name) and the Filipino bands BINI and SB19.
Elsewhere, Beyoncé picked up the 100th nomination of her career when Morning Dew (Donk) was shortlisted for best R&B solo performance.
Songs and albums had to be released between 31 August 2025 and 28 August 2026 to qualify for nominations.
body_zh: 2027 年格莱美奖：雷伊 (Raye) 获得 11 项提名领先，多莉·帕顿 (Dolly Parton) 获得死后提名 - BBC 新闻
英国歌手 Raye 在即将举行的格莱美奖中以 11 项提名领跑，而多莉·帕顿 (Dolly Parton) 则在死后获得了 3 项提名。
Raye 凭借她最新的水星奖获奖唱片《This Album May Contain Hope》及其主打单曲《Where Is My Husband!》获得提名，该单曲同时入围年度歌曲和年度唱片奖。
其他提名者包括罗莎莉亚、埃拉·兰利、奥利维亚·迪恩、爱莉安娜·格兰德、布鲁诺·马尔斯、泰勒·斯威夫特、奥利维亚·罗德里戈、米兰达·兰伯特和菲比·布里杰斯。
帕顿在这位乡村音乐明星 80 岁去世三个月后获得了两项最佳乡村二重奏/团体表演类别的提名。
帕顿因与扎克·布朗乐队合作的《蝴蝶》、《清蓝晨光》以及包括她的教女麦莉·赛勒斯在内的全明星阵容而受到认可。
这位已故的乡村明星还因其对《表演之星：我的舞台生活》的旁白而获得最佳有声读物提名。
2027 年格莱美颁奖典礼将于 2 月 7 日星期日在洛杉矶举行。
请访问格莱美官方网站、外部查看完整提名名单
麦当娜的专辑《Confessions II》是 2005 年《Confessions on a Dancefloor》的续集，没有出现在“四大”类别中——包括年度专辑、年度唱片和年度歌曲。
许多人认为格莱美奖延续了冷落这位美国歌手的传统，但这张专辑确实进入了最佳舞曲类别。
罗莎莉亚 (Rosalía) 凭借广受好评的专辑《Lux》获得九项提名，此前她在上周的拉丁格莱美奖上取得了巨大成功。
兰利的七项提名包括她突破性的热门歌曲《Choosin' Texas》的年度歌曲提名，该歌曲今年成为公告牌百强单曲榜历史上持续时间最长的单曲。
引入了五个新类别，包括最佳拉丁歌曲和最佳亚洲流行音乐表演。
加入它们是学院尝试使活动“更具包容性”并代表更广泛的音乐流派的一部分。
然而，批评者担心，新的专业类别将导致韩国流行音乐等流派在主要类别中的代表性不足，而包括 BTS 和 Stray Kids 在内的艺人表示，他们将抵制明年的颁奖典礼。
韩国五家最大的娱乐公司中有四家拒绝考虑他们的音乐。 Starship Entertainment逆势而上，旗下女子乐队IVE和KiiiKiii获得提名。
其他提名者包括 Babymetal、日本歌手 Lisa（不要与 Blackpink 的同名明星混淆）以及菲律宾乐队 BINI 和 SB19。
在其他地方，碧昂丝 (Beyoncé) 凭借《Morning Dew》(Donk) 入围最佳 R&B 独奏表演奖，获得了她职业生涯中的第 100 次提名。
歌曲和专辑必须在2025年8月31日至2026年8月28日之间发行才有资格获得提名。

title_en: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction
title_zh: 杰拉尔·德帕迪约放弃对性侵犯定罪的上诉
summary: The French film star was due to start an appeal trial after being found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a Paris set.
summary_zh: 这位法国电影明星在巴黎片场性侵两名女性的罪名被判有罪后，将开始上诉审判。
body_en: French film star Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexual assault , admitting that his behaviour towards women had often been offensive and offering a "deep and sincere" apology.
On the day that the appeal was due to start in a Paris court, the 77-year-old actor's unexpected mea culpa marks a dramatic reversal of his previous denials of sexual impropriety.
"Justice was pronounced. I was found guilty. I understand and bow to this conviction… I have therefore decided to abandon the appeal," he wrote.
It means he is now guilty in law of abusing two women during a film shoot in Paris five years ago, and his 18-month suspended prison term stands.
"Victory is ours, and we welcome it with head held high," said one of the two women, named only as Amélie, who was at the court.
"There is huge relief because the fight is over. The giant of film has fallen," said the other woman in the case, who is known in court by the false name Sarah.
In his statement, Depardieu appeared to have undergone a major shift from his earlier stance of unapologetic intransigence.
"For a long time on film shoots I hid myself behind provocation and smut. I thought that the remarks I made, and certain gestures that I made, were of no consequence.

"I see now that there is a border between impertinence and offence. Never, ever did I intend to hurt the women with whom I came into contact. But I see now that intention has no bearing on the hurt that people feel.

"Cases before the courts are damaging. Everything got out of hand… including my defence. Many people have suffered in this story. I have not the power to go back in time. I have come to understand that I belonged to a world that has disappeared."
The reference to his defence "getting out of hand" follows widespread criticism of the aggressive line taken by Depardieu's lawyer during the original trial in March last year.

His new lawyers, Delphine Meillet and David-Olivier Kaminski, said that with his admission of guilt Depardieu wanted to "move on", adding that "basically, as he turns 78 years old, he is saying to himself that life is more beautiful than 10 days of court hearings".

In the original trial, Depardieu was said to have touched the two women on intimate parts of the body during the making of Les Volets Verts, which is a film about an ageing actor coming to terms with his declining powers.
He himself admitted to using vulgar language but denied being "a metro-train groper". However, he also said he did not consider touching a woman's buttocks to be an act of "sexual aggression".
The trial was the first time the star of films like Green Card and Cyrano de Bergerac appeared in court on sexual assault charges. Several other women have made similar allegations in the media.
A decision on whether an alleged rape case can come to trial is expected this month.

body_zh: 法国电影明星杰拉尔·德帕迪约 (Gérard Depardieu) 放弃了对性侵犯定罪的上诉，承认自己对女性的行为经常具有冒犯性，并做出了“深切而真诚的”道歉。
在巴黎法院开始上诉的当天，这位 77 岁的演员出人意料地道歉，这标志着他之前否认不当性行为的戏剧性逆转。
“正义得到了伸张。我被判有罪。我理解并接受这一判决……因此我决定放弃上诉，”他写道。
这意味着他现在因五年前在巴黎拍摄电影时虐待两名女性而被判有罪，18 个月的缓刑仍然有效。
“胜利是我们的，我们昂首阔步地欢迎它，”法庭上的两名女子之一说道，她的名字只叫阿梅莉。
“大家都松了口气，因为战斗已经结束。电影巨人已经倒下了，”该案中的另一名女性说，她在法庭上化名莎拉。
在他的声明中，德帕迪约似乎与之前毫无歉意的顽固立场发生了重大转变。
“在拍摄电影的很长一段时间里，我都把自己隐藏在挑衅和猥亵的背后。我认为我发表的言论和我做出的某些手势无关紧要。
“我现在明白，无礼和冒犯之间存在界限。我从来没有打算伤害与我接触过的女性。但我现在明白，这种意图与人们感受到的伤害无关。
“法庭上的案件具有破坏性。一切都失控了……包括我的辩护。很多人在这个故事中受苦。我没有能力回到过去。我开始明白，我属于一个已经消失的世界。”
在提到他的辩护“失控”之前，德帕迪约的律师在去年三月的初审中采取的激进路线受到了广泛的批评。
他的新律师德尔菲娜·梅莱特（Delphine Meil​​let）和大卫-奥利维尔·卡明斯基（David-Olivier Kaminski）表示，德帕迪约认罪后希望“继续前进”，并补充说，“基本上，当他78岁的时候，他对自己说，生活比十天的法庭听证会更美好”。
在最初的审判中，据说德帕迪约在拍摄《绿色的翅膀》期间触摸了这两名女性的私密部位，该片讲述了一位年老演员接受自己日渐衰弱的能力的故事。
他本人承认使用粗俗语言，但否认自己是“地铁骚扰者”。不过，他也表示，他不认为触摸女性臀部是一种“性侵犯”行为。
此次审判是这位《绿卡》和《西拉诺·德·贝热拉克》等电影明星首次因性侵犯指控出庭。其他几位女性也在媒体上提出了类似的指控。
预计本月将就涉嫌强奸案是否可以接受审判做出决定。
